meaning: The client's claimed identity. Match it against agents.json, then http-clients.json.

Browsers never rank text/markdown or text/x-markdown above text/html, and never rank text/plain first. A request that prefers markdown comes from AI tooling. Some tools send a distinctive Accept string, listed under an agent's accept field.
Names the operator of a Web Bot Auth signed request, e.g. chatgpt.com. It is a claim until the Signature and Signature-Input headers are verified against that operator's key directory.
RFC 9421 HTTP message signature. Proves the operator when it validates against the key directory in agents.json verify.webBotAuth.
usedBy: classify, as a requirement for using signature-agent

meaning: Signature parameters. Web Bot Auth requests use tag="web-bot-auth".
usedBy: classify, as a requirement for using signature-agent

meaning: Every current browser sends sec-fetch-mode, sec-fetch-site and sec-fetch-dest on HTTPS requests. A browser user agent without them is not a browser.
usedBy: classify, only when headersComplete is true

meaning: Sent by Chromium-based browsers only. On a Firefox or Safari user agent it means the user agent is fake.
usedBy: classify, only when headersComplete is true

meaning: Browsers always send it. Its absence on a browser user agent points to automation.
usedBy: classify, only when headersComplete is true

meaning: Some crawlers put a contact address here. Its presence points to automation.
The real client IP when you sit behind Cloudflare. Use your own proxy's header for IP verification; never the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value, which the client can set.
